newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended mixed after trading narrowly in moderate activity ahead of Friday's expiry of the near October contract. October closed $0.80 higher at $346.40. A steady volume of trade switching of short positions from October to December and March helped to keep the market in a tight range. In New York raw sugar futures ended mixed with front month October losing 7 points to close at 11.89 cents/lb, while March closed one point higher at 11.67 cents/lb. The back months closed one point lower to 2 points higher. Liquidation of October and March contracts and speculators rolling long positions into March ahead of the October contract's expiry pressured prices. Otherwise trading was very quiet with no fresh fundamental news giving the market direction.

INDIA - Sugar production in India from 1 October to 15 August 1995/96 reached 16.325 million tonnes, white value, up from 14.417 million tonnes produced the same period in 1994/95. Consumption up to 15 August reached 11.407 million tonnes, 6.76 per cent up on last year's figure. Exports up to 15 August totalled 911,000 tonnes against a mere 23,000 tonnes the same period in 1994/95. Stocks on 15 August rose significantly to 9.605 million tonnes up from 6.797 million tonnes the previous year. 26 factories were working as of August 15, 1996 as against 33 at the same date last season. Against contracts for one million tonnes, the ISIEC has so far physically shipped 742,923 tonnes to: Maldives 1,925 tonnes, Somalia 2,000 tonnes, Aden 2,200 tonnes, Burma 13,500 tonnes, Eritrea 12,500 tonnes, Yemen 17,500 tonnes, Russia 90,000 tonnes, Sri Lanka 180,013 tonnes, Indonesia 205,811 tonnes, Kenya 29,500 tonnes, Bangladesh 35,758 tonnes and Pakistan 152,216 tonnes. Total production in 1995/96 is now estimated at 16.405 million tonnes and is likely to come down to 15.575 million tonnes in 1996/97. In the largest producing state Maharashtra output is forecast to fall from 5.393 million tonnes to 4.800 million tonnes.

MAN - London trade house E.D.&F. Man said in its latest monthly sugar report that the EU should produce 15.29 million tonnes of sugar, white value, from its 1996/97 beet crop, down almost 374,000 tonnes on last year. Our own estimate for 1996/97, released some time ago, was at 15.168 million tonnes. Man said cold and dry spring weather in northern Europe caused delays in early beet development and the summer drought had also dampened expectations.

AUSTRALIA - Sugar exports in July 1996 hit 693,582 tonnes, raw value, the highest tonnage ever shipped in this month. This brought cumulative exports in the first two months of the 1996/97 campaign (June/July) up to 830,861 tonnes, 17.1 percent up on the previous year's 709,478 tonnes. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 4.17 million tonnes, down from 4.48 million tonnes in 1994. Major countries of destination in June/July 1996 were Canada with 155,350 tonnes raws against 98,258 tonnes, Malaysia with 150,050 tonnes compared to 139,545 tonnes and Japan with 91,054 tonnes down from 129,670 tonnes. Furthermore, Australia continues to serve the markets in Eastern Europe and Northern Africa. Bulgaria received 25,000 tonnes of raws while another 43,000 tonnes were shipped to Egypt in June/July 1996. White sugar exports in June/July 1996 amounted to 34,316 tonnes, slightly up on last year's 33,553 tonnes. Major white sugar destinations were Sri Lanka with 19,500 tonnes compared to 5,489 tonnes and Hongkong with 5,605 tonnes compared to 5,033 tonnes.

UNITED STATES - Sugar imports under the 1995/96 (October/September) tariff rate quota up to September 8, 1996 amounted to 1,616,331 tonnes, raw value. This is equivalent to 74.58 per cent of the total quota of 2.17 million tonnes.

UKRAINE - The fourth Ukrainian beet test of September 13, 1996 showed a good increase in both sugar and beet yields although the overall results are still disappointing. Beet yield on September 13 reached 22.28 tonnes per ha, down from 25.42 tonnes in 1994 and the 1994 result of 24.61 tonnes. Sugar content was no more than 14.6 percent, down from 15.3 percent in 1995 and 16.1 percent in 1994. This resulted in a theoretical sugar weight of 3.25 tonnes per ha, 16.5 percent down on the 1995 result of 3.89 tonnes. According to Leonid Bershtein, deputy director of Ukraine's Sugar Research Institute, the 1996 campaign has already begun. Total beet production is forecast at 26 million tonnes, down from 30 million in 1995. Bershtein added yields for the entire crop would probably be less than 20 tonnes per ha, compared to 21.9 tonnes in 1995. Real sugar content at the factory would probably be no more than 12 percent. Government forecasts put sugar output for this year at 2.8 to 3.0 million tonnes, white value, down from last year's 3.485 million tonnes.

Jordan is seeking to buy 30,000 tonnes of white refined or white crystal sugar for delivery in the second-half of November and first half of December, traders said. The shipment is to be delivered in two lots of 15,000 tonnes each, the first lot during the second-half November and the second by first-half December, it was added. Offers must be received by Jordan's Ministry of supply by October 2. The state-run Trading Corp of Pakistan (TCP) is likely to invite bids in the next few days for the import of 50,000 tonnes of crystal white sugar, an official of the corporation said. The TCP had so far purchased 225,000 tonnes of sugar mainly from India on a government-to-government level, the official said. The private sector had also imported some sugar but the quantities involved were not known, it was added. According to trade sources, more than six cargoes of sugar had been booked by the private sector for delivery by October.
